# Swarm

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Swarm")`

Steers a large crowd of agents on open ground, such as a horde of hundreds. The agents walk toward `Target`, push each other apart, follow the height of the terrain and go around the obstacles the swarm was given. When the way is blocked, they climb over the agent in front and stand on the agents under them.

An agent is not an instance. It is an entry the swarm keeps, with a radius, a height and a speed. It moves one body, the `BasePart` given to `AddAgent`, which the swarm places every tick facing `Target`. Scripts add, remove, push and query agents in bulk, and no Luau code runs per agent.

The swarm updates every simulation tick, after `PreSimulation`, and is deterministic. An agent far from `Target` is updated less often: every second tick beyond `NearDistance` and every fourth beyond `FarDistance`, moving by the time it skipped.

For agents that follow paths on a navigation mesh, use `NavigationAgent`.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CellSize` | `number` | `1.5` | read/write | The side of the cells of the grid in which agents find their neighbors, in meters. Set it to about the diameter of the widest agent. |
| `ClimbSpeed` | `number` | `6` | read/write | The speed at which an agent climbs over the agent in its way, in meters per second. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the swarm updates. When it is off, its agents stay where they are. |
| `FarDistance` | `number` | `48` | read/write | The distance from `Target`, in meters, beyond which an agent is updated every fourth tick. |
| `Gravity` | `number` | `30` | read/write | The acceleration at which an agent falls, in meters per second squared. |
| `MaxNeighbors` | `number` | `14` | read/write | The largest number of neighbors an agent considers each tick. It limits the cost of a tightly packed crowd. |
| `MaxNeighbours` | `number` | — | deprecated | Deprecated: use `MaxNeighbors`. The old name still works. |
| `NearDistance` | `number` | `24` | read/write | The distance from `Target`, in meters, beyond which an agent is updated every second tick. |
| `PileHeight` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How high the crowd can pile on itself, in meters above the ground under an agent. 0 means no limit.<br><br>Above this height, an agent does not climb the agent in its way, and an agent standing on one that tall is pushed aside and comes down. A limit of two or three agents' heights looks like a wave breaking over an obstacle. With no limit, a crowd around a stationary obstacle builds a tower over it. |
| `Replicates` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the swarm's agents are replicated to the other machines in a multiplayer match. When it is on, each client has this swarm with the same agent numbers, read-only. On a client, `GetAgents`, `GetPositions`, `GetAgentPosition`, `GetAgentTag` and `QueryRadius` return results, `AgentAdded`, `AgentRemoved` and `AgentTagChanged` fire, and `SetAgentBody` gives an agent a local body to move.<br><br>An agent's state is sent to a client when the client's copy would otherwise be drawn wrong, and the client moves the agent itself in between. A client's agent is therefore close to the authority's position but not exactly at it; decide hits on the authority. A client has only the agents within `ReplicationRadius` of its player's focus.<br><br>When it is off, the swarm exists only on the machine that runs it. |
| `ReplicationRadius` | `number` | `80` | read/write | The distance from a player's focus, in meters, within which agents are sent to that player's machine. The focus is the player's `Character`, or `Player.ReplicationFocus`. An agent that leaves the radius is removed on that machine (`AgentRemoved` with `OutOfReach`) and added again when it returns. |
| `StopDistance` | `number` | `0.55` | read/write | The distance from `Target`, beyond the agent's own radius, at which an agent stops walking toward it. |
| `Target` | `vector` | — | read/write | The position every agent walks toward, unless `SetTargets` has given other targets. |

## Methods

### `AddAgent(body: BasePart, settings: { Radius: number?, Height: number?, Speed: number?, Floats: boolean?, FloatHeight: number?, Climbs: boolean? }?): number`

Adds an agent at the position of `body` and returns its number. The options are `Radius` (default 0.5), `Height` (1) and `Speed` (4, in meters per second). `Floats` keeps the agent `FloatHeight` (1) above the ground, where the crowd does not push it. `Climbs` (true) lets it climb over the agent in its way.

The number identifies the agent while it exists and is reused for a later agent after this one is removed. For an agent with no body, use `AddAgentAt`.

### `AddAgentAt(position: vector, settings: { Radius: number?, Height: number?, Speed: number?, Floats: boolean?, FloatHeight: number?, Climbs: boolean? }?): number`

Adds an agent that has no body, with its feet at `position`, and returns its number. The swarm simulates it and nothing is drawn. Use it on a server that simulates a horde for clients that draw it themselves: read the agents with `GetPositions` and send what the clients need. The options are those of `AddAgent`.

### `AddObstacle(position: vector, radius: number)`

Adds an obstacle that agents walk around, such as a tree or a rock, as a circle on the ground.

### `ClearObstacles()`

Removes every obstacle.

### `GetAgentPosition(agent: number): vector?`

Returns the position of an agent, or nil if there is no such agent.

### `GetAgentTag(agent: number): number`

Returns an agent's tag. Returns 0 for an agent that was never given one, or that does not exist.

### `GetAgents(into: { number }?): { number }`

Returns the number of every live agent, in slot order. If `into` is given, that table is cleared, filled and returned, so a script that calls this every tick allocates nothing.

### `GetPositions(into: { vector }?): { vector }`

Returns the position of every live agent, in the order `GetAgents` returns them. If `into` is given, that table is cleared, filled and returned.

### `Push(agent: number, velocity: vector)`

Knocks an agent back with a velocity along the ground, in meters per second, that fades quickly.

### `QueryRadius(center: vector, radius: number, into: { number }?, flat: boolean?): { number }`

Returns every live agent whose feet are within `radius` of `center`, in slot order. Use it to find what a weapon hits, or which agents have reached `Target`. Its cost depends on the number of agents near `center`, not on the size of the swarm.

If `into` is given, that table is cleared, filled and returned. With `flat`, distance is measured along the ground only, so every agent of a pile above the circle is included.

### `RemoveAgent(agent: number)`

Removes an agent from the swarm. Its body stays where it is and is no longer moved.

### `SetAgentBody(agent: number, body: BasePart?)`

Gives an agent a part on this machine to move, or nil to release it. Every tick the swarm sets the part's `CFrame` to the agent's position, facing its target, and changes nothing else about the part.

On the authority, it replaces the body given to `AddAgent`. On a client, it is how a replicated horde is drawn: create a body when `AgentAdded` fires, pass it here, and take it back when `AgentRemoved` fires. The part is drawn interpolated between ticks like any moving part.

### `SetAgentPosition(agent: number, position: vector)`

Moves an agent to a position. It falls to the ground from there.

### `SetAgentSpeed(agent: number, speed: number)`

Sets how fast an agent walks, in meters per second. At 0 the agent stays in place, and other agents still push it.

### `SetAgentTag(agent: number, tag: number)`

Sets an agent's tag: an integer from 0 to 65535 whose meaning the game defines, for example a kind in some bits and flags in others. Only the authority can call it.

The tag replicates to every machine that has the agent. Those machines read it with `GetAgentTag` and receive `AgentTagChanged`; a client typically chooses a mesh and a pose from it. The tag an agent has when it is removed is sent with the removal, so a "killed" flag set just before `RemoveAgent` reaches every machine's `AgentRemoved`.

### `SetTargets(targets: { vector })`

Sets several positions for the agents to walk toward, such as every player in a match. Each agent walks toward the nearest one, and its update rate (`NearDistance`, `FarDistance`) depends on its distance to that one. Call it again whenever the positions change. An empty table goes back to using `Target` alone.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `AgentAdded(agent: number, tag: number, size: vector)`

Fires when this machine gains an agent. On the authority that is after `AddAgent`; on a client it is when an agent arrives, either newly created or entering the client's replication radius. `size` is the agent's width, height and width again. The number identifies the agent on every machine until `AgentRemoved` fires for it, and can be reused after that.

### `AgentRemoved(agent: number, tag: number, position: vector, reason: Enum.SwarmAgentRemoval)`

Fires when this machine loses an agent. Passes the agent's last tag and position, and the reason: the authority removed it, or, on a client, it left the client's replication radius. Play a death effect for the first reason and nothing for the second.

### `AgentTagChanged(agent: number, tag: number)`

Fires when the tag of an agent that this machine has changes.
